### PackedSelection: Memory-Efficient Boolean Selections

Source: https://context7.com/scikit-hep/coffea/llms.txt

PackedSelection efficiently stores multiple per-event boolean flags in a single integer array using bitwise operations. It supports eager and delayed modes and provides methods for combining selections like all(), any(), require(), cutflow(), and nminusone().

```python
import numpy as np
import awkward as ak
from coffea.analysis_tools import PackedSelection

events_n = 100_000
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
pt  = rng.exponential(30, events_n)
eta = rng.uniform(-3, 3, events_n)
iso = rng.uniform(0, 1, events_n) < 0.85

sel = PackedSelection(dtype="uint32")
sel.add("pt_cut",  pt  > 25)
sel.add("eta_cut", np.abs(eta) < 2.4)
sel.add("iso_cut", iso)

# Require all three cuts
all_cuts = sel.all("pt_cut", "eta_cut", "iso_cut")
print(f"Pass all: {all_cuts.sum()}")

# Require pt and eta but NOT iso (to study iso efficiency)
anti_iso = sel.require(pt_cut=True, eta_cut=True, iso_cut=False)

# Sequential cutflow
cf = sel.cutflow("pt_cut", "eta_cut", "iso_cut")
cf.print()
# Cutflow selection stats:
#   Cut pt_cut :  pass = 68214   cumulative pass = 68214   ...
#   Cut eta_cut:  pass = 52190   cumulative pass = 46321   ...
#   Cut iso_cut:  pass = 85012   cumulative pass = 39381   ...

# N-1 analysis
nm1 = sel.nminusone("pt_cut", "eta_cut", "iso_cut")
nm1.print()
# N-1 selection stats:
#   Ignoring pt_cut   pass = 42150  all = 100000  -- eff = 42.2 %
#   ...

```
